Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 8, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES

CALL TO ORDER AT 6:33 P.M.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

PRESENT: Mayor Murdock, Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi, Council Member Kemps, and Council
  Member Roos

ABSENT:  Council Member Kemps

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Kallman, City Attorney Rusin, City Clerk Cook,
  Community Development Director Brady, Acting Public Works Director
  Wieske, Chief Hellinga, and City Treasurer Greenberg

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi and Seconded by Council Member
  McGowan to approve the agenda.

AYES: Murdock, Lozzi, Roos, McGowan
NOES: None
ABSENT: Kemps

MAYOR’S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Mayor Murdock reported out on the litigation settlement for the lawsuit regarding claims of
localism in Lunada Bay. She informed residents details of the settlement are available on
the city’s website. She reiterated the city’s commitment to preserving the natural look and
feel of the area. Regarding fire safety, the mayor reported on a small fire that occurred in
Valmonte and reminded residents they need to make sure their vegetation does not grow
into or near the electrical wires as this was the cause.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 8, 2024
 In her “Did You Know” segment, Mayor Murdock shared that street sweeping is part of the
city’s contract with Athens and that sweeping occurs on Fridays. Commercial areas are
done weekly and residential streets are swept monthly. To find out when your street is
scheduled for sweeping, go on the city’s website to Services/Public Works and scroll down
towards the bottom. She reminded residents to try to not park on their street when it is
scheduled for sweeping and to keep vegetation maintained so it is not in the gutter or
overhanging the curb.

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Kallman reminded residents that Geosyntec will be performing testing along
Via Corta and the road behind City Hall the week of 10/21 and there will be road closures
for three days.

Chief Hellinga announced a new pilot where trained PSA (police service aides) will be
enforcing municipal codes such as gas leaf blowers and business licenses. He also
reminded the public of the breast cancer awareness pink patches which are for sale with
proceeds to go to an officer in Inglewood battling breast cancer.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Council was addressed by Valerie Gorsuch, Craig Quinn, Joan Davidson, and Lucy Padilla.

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1-8)

City Attorney Rusin announced a change in the staff recommendation for item #4 which is
that Items #1 and #4 be returned to the Parklands Committee for clarification and for these
items to be reported back to Council at a future time. Only items #2 and #3 on tonight’s
Parklands Committee minutes would be addressed tonight.

Council was addressed by Sally and Kirby Larson, Ruth MacFarlane and Monique
Thorington regarding item #4.

ACTION: Moved by Council Member Roos and Seconded by Council Member
  McGowan to approve the consent agenda items with the clarification of only
  items #2 & 3 on the Parklands Committee action minutes (item #4 on tonight’s
  agenda).

AYES: Murdock, Lozzi, Roos, McGowan
NOES: None
ABSENT: Kemps

1.  APPROVAL OF WARRANTS

  Reviewed and Approved Warrant Register of October 8, 2024.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 8, 2024
 2.  RECEIVE AND FILE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE PERIOD ENDING
  AUGUST 31, 2024

  Received and Filed the financial statements for the month ending August 31,
  2024.

3.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS

  Approved the minutes for the following meeting: September 10, 2024

4.  PARKLAND COMMITTEE MEETING ACTIONS

  Approved the action minutes for the Parklands Committee meeting of
  September 12, 2024 (Items #2 and #3, returned #1 and #4 to Parklands).

5.  2025 PALOS VERDES TENNIS CLUB BUDGET

  Approved the proposed 2025 budget for the Palos Verdes Tennis Club.

6.  CONSIDER THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH TRIPEPI, SMITH AND ASSOCIATES, INC. TO CONTINUE TO
  PROVIDE COMMUNICATION SERVICES FOR THE REMAINDER OF THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2024-2025

  Approved the second amendment to the professional services agreement with
  Tripepi, Smith and Associates, Inc. (“Tripepi”) to increase the compensation
  amount to a not-to-exceed amount of $140,000.

7.  ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE THE SUBMITTAL OF
  APPLICATIONS FOR MEASURE A FUNDS AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY
  MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE MEASURE A ANNUAL ALLOCATION
  AGREEMENT AND GRANT RELATED DOCUMENTS

City Council:
  1.  Adopted a resolution to allow the City of Palos Verdes Estates (City) to apply
  for Measure A grant funds

  2.  Approved the Measure A Annual Allocation Agreement (Agreement) and

  3.  Authorized the City Manager or designees as signatories, to execute all
  Measure A program-related documents

8.  SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION OF THE LUNADA BAY HOMEOWNERS
  ASSOCIATION TO HOLD ITS HARVEST FESTIVAL AT LUNADA BAY PARK ON
  OCTOBER 27, 2024

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 8, 2024
   Approved the Special Event Application submitted by the Lunada Bay
  Homeowners Association to host the LBHOA Harvest Festival on Sunday,
  October 27, 2024, from 2:00PM to 6:00PM at Lunada Bay Park and the adjacent
  street of Via Anacapa.

NEW BUSINESS

9.  CONSIDER AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE AGREEMENT WITH BENNETT
  LANDSCAPING TO MODIFY THE ANNUAL NOT TO EXCEED AMOUNT OF
  $1,506,746 TO $1,423,224 FOR YEAR 1; APPROVE A ONE-YEAR EXTENSION
  FOR CITYWIDE LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,423,224
  FOR YEAR 2; AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXTEND THE CONTRACT
  FOR AN ADDITIONAL TWO, ONE-YEAR EXTENSIONS SUBJECT OT CIPI
  ADJUSTMENTS EACH YEAR; AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  EXECUTE AMENDMENT NO. 2 IN FINAL FORM AND FORMAT AS APPROVED BY
  THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  City Engineer Loriso provided a staff report. Council asked clarifying questions. Sean
  Bennett from Bennett Landscaping responded to Council questions. City Manager
  Kallman reported that at the advice of the City Attorney, Staff is recommending that
  Council provide feedback and direction, and Staff will bring the item back on consent
  at a future meeting. Council raised concerns regarding city maintenance of ROWs
  adjacent to private property, clearance of vegetative encroachments onto public land,
  overlaps with the BATS contract, lack of progress on gopher control, and
  implementation of a CPI adjustment ahead of what is in the current contract.

  There was no public comment.

10. CONSIDERATION AND PROPOSED APPROVAL OF RESOLUTIONS R24-54, R24-
  55, AND R24-56 BETWEEN THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES AND THE
  PROFESSIONAL & SUPERVISORY, MANAGEMENT ADMINISTRATION, AND
  SWORN POLICE MANAGEMENT GROUPS. APPROVAL AND CREATION OF A
  DEPUTY CITY MANAGER POSITION.

  City Manager Kallman provided a staff report. Council asked clarifying questions.

  There was no public comment.

  Council provided direction to Staff to conduct a Class & Comp Study.

ACTION: Moved by Council Member McGowan and Seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi
  to adopt the resolutions with the following changes: eliminate any retroactivity
  and make any changes effective the date the resolutions are adopted, to cap
  PD management sick leave at 1000 hours like all other employee groups, and
  to remove the option for monetary compensation in lieu of a city phone.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 8, 2024
 AYES: Lozzi, Roos, McGowan
NOES: Murdock
ABSENT: Kemps

Council recessed for a break at 8:29 P.M. and returned at 8:40 P.M.

11. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION TO AWARD A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT TO NV5, INC. FOR THE DESIGN OF STRUCTURAL REPAIRS FOR
  THE EXISTING RETAINING WALL ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE WEST IN AN
  AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $199,220; APPROVE ADDITIONAL EXPENDITURES
  NOT TO EXCEED $20,000, WHICH IS APPROXIMATELY 10% OF THE CONTRACT
  AMOUNT; AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE ALL CONTRACT
  DOCUMENTS IN THE FINAL FORM AND FORMAT AS APPROVED BY THE CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  City Engineer provided a staff report. Council asked clarifying questions.

  There was no public comment.

ACTION: Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi and Seconded by Council Member McGowan
  to adopt the resolution R24-50 to award professional services agreement to
  NV5 for the design of structural repairs PW-704-23 for an amount not to exceed
  $199,220, to approve additional expenditures not to exceed $20,000 which is
  10% of the contract amount, and to authorize the city manager to execute all
  contract documents in the final format as approved by the city attorney.

AYES: Murdock, Lozzi, Roos, McGowan
NOES: None
ABSENT: Kemps

12. CONSIDER REJECTING ALL PROPOSALS RECEIVED FOR THE MASTER PLAN
  OF STORM DRAIN AND CONSIDER IMMEDIATE DRAINAGE PROJECT NEEDS.

  City Engineer Loriso provided a staff report, clarified that all storm drains were not
  intended to be videotaped but only hot spots identified during development of the
  master plan, and explained the recommendation to reject the bids was based on
  their coming in over what was budgeted in the CIP. Council asked clarifying
  questions.

  There was no public comment.

  Council provided direction to Staff to work to keep the bids “live” for a longer time
  period and to return with a list of immediate storm drain repairs needed in the event
  Council wants to pursue both paths. Council continued this item to a date to be
  determined.

OLD BUSINESS

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 8, 2024
 13. MALAGA LANE WATER INTRUSION AND SUBSURFACE INVESTIGATION

  City Engineer Loriso provided a staff report on the latest ground penetration radar
  work performed in the area and any future work planned. Council asked clarifying
  questions. Yonas from Geosyntec was available to answer questions.

  Council was addressed by Sylvia Dachterman and Lucy Padilla.

ACTION: Moved by Council Member McGowan and Seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi
  to declare a local emergency, authorize the Proclamation, and authorize staff
  to spend up to $100,000 as needed to remediate the sink holes along Malaga
  Lane.

AYES: Murdock, Lozzi, Roos, McGowan
NOES: None
ABSENT: Kemps

MAYOR AND COUNCILMEMBER REPORTS & TENTATIVE FUTURE AGENDA

Mayor Murdock reported she attended the September SBCCOG meeting in place of Mayor
Pro Tem Lozzi.

Council Member Roos announced he is moving next week to Austin, Texas and that it has
been a pleasure to serve the city for the past seven years, including on Planning
Commission. He reminded us he was Mayor once. He handed Mayor Murdock his letter of
resignation which is effective 11:59 P.M. October 17, 2024. Council members thanked Jim
Ross for his service and expressed their appreciation for his service.

ADJOURNMENT TO TUESDAY, OCTOBER 22, 2024, AT 6:30 P.M.
Meeting was adjourned at 9:38 P.M.

Respectfully submitted:

________________________________
Tameka Cook, City Clerk

  APPROVED:

  _______________________________
  Dawn Murdock, Mayor

   MINUTES OF THE OCTOBER 22, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES

CALL TO ORDER AT 6:30 P.M.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ROLL CALL
PRESENT: Mayor Murdock, Mayor Pro Tem Lozzi, Council Member Kemps, Council
  Member McGowan

ALSO PRESENT: City Manager Kallman, City Attorney Rusin, City Clerk Cook, Community
  Development Director Brady, City Engineer Loriso, Chief Hellinga, and City

APPROVAL OF AGENDA
ACTION:  Moved by Mayor Murdock and Seconded by Council Member Kemps to move

NOES: None

CEREMONIAL PRESENTATIONS

LIFE SAVING AWARD – Chief Hellinga presented life savings awards to Acting Sergeant
Sean Crisfield, Officer Neil Sisson, Firefighter Paramedics Derrick Ho, Frank Guitierrez, and
Alan Matsumoto, and PVPUSD Registered Nurse Ralista “Railli” Berkovski-Varbanov

PROCLAMATION: Honoring Eleazar “Alic” Abrego Upon His Retirement – Mayor Murdock
read a proclamation thanking Alic for his 43 years of service. City Manager Kallman and
Anthony Mendoza provided comments regarding Alic’s works and thanked him for his service
and awarded him with a custom shirt and street sign.

MAYOR’S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Mayor Murdock announced Council Member Roos’ resignation due to a move to Austin Texas
and stated council will not be filling the seat as a new council will be in place in December.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 22, 2024
 She thanked him for his service and sense of humor. The Mayor shared she attended the
Friday night homecoming game at PVHS and thanked residents for their patience and
understanding while putting up with the accompanying inconveniences that come with the
annual homecoming activities. She reminded the public of the upcoming joint meeting with
the Planning Commission on October 30, 2024 to discuss the draft comprehensive objective
design standards, that the Lunada Bay Harvest Festival is October 27 from 2-6 P.M., and to
vote on November 5.

In her “Did You Know” segment, Mayor Murdock noted seeing houses placing trash cans at
the curb. She reminded residents that PVE Municipal Codes 8.16.020 and 8.16.090 state
trash cans need to be concealed and on private property and doing otherwise is a code
violation.

CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Kallman reminded residents of Sunday’s Prepared Peninsula Expo at Peninsula
High School from 10 A.M. to 1 P.M. He thanked Anthony Mendoza and John Strum for their
after-hours service to address fallen trees.

City Clerk Cook provided information related to the upcoming election and the various
locations and hours of operation to vote in person and submit mail-in ballots.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC
Council was addressed by Christine Fine, Phyllis Scribe, Valerie Gorsuch, John Weick, Parvin
Jensen, Darcel Rameriz-Hanson, and Terry Pearson.

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEMS 1-10)

There was no public comment.

5.  CONSIDER AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE AGREEMENT WITH BENNETT

  $1,506,746 TO $1,386,406 FOR YEAR 1; APPROVE A ONE-YEAR EXTENSION FOR
  CITYWIDE LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE IN THE AMOUNT OF $1,386,406 FOR
  YEAR 2; AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER THE OPTION TO EXTEND THE
  CONTRACT FOR AN ADDITIONAL TWO, ONE-YEAR EXTENSIONS SUBJECT TO
  CPI ADJUSTMENTS STARTING YEAR 4; AND AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER
  TO EXECUTE AMENDMENT NO.2.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 22, 2024
   Mayor Murdock expressed concerns that the six issues she brought up at the October
  8 discussion on this item were not addressed. Council asked additional clarifying
  questions. Staff and Sean Bennett of Bennett Landscaping responded.

  Council expressed the need to provide more information to the public regarding the
  use of herbicides to both educate and inform. Information needs to be on the city
  website and bi-weekly updates and include information on when and where herbicides
  will be used and a set of FAQs to address residents’ concerns including the safety of
  products. Council also directed Staff to provide an annual presentation on how the
  contract is doing relative to our goals.

  Council was addressed by Darcel Ramirez-Hanson.

  ACTION: Moved by Council Member McGowan and Seconded by Council Member
  Kemps to approve the contract as staff has proposed, that staff, on an annual
  basis, review the progress against our milestones and goals of the contract
  including the use of pesticides, and that the City Manager find ways to
  communicate these pertinent facts to our residents.

  AYES: Lozzi, Kemps, McGowan
  NOES: Murdock

  Malaga Lane have been filled with slurry at a cost within the amount approved by
  Council. Council asked clarifying questions. City Manager Kallman provided an update
  regarding the Steering Committee meetings and options Staff is investigating. Council
  expressed a desire to ensure all affected property owners are aware of the City’s efforts.
  It was suggested a post card be sent to all owners informing them Council is discussing
